sources: Stephens, Atkins & Kingston (2009). Swearing as a response to pain. NeuroReport 20(12). 67 undergraduates (38 men, 29 women), cold-pressor task; mean latency swearing vs neutral: men 190.6 vs 146.7 s, women 120.3 vs 83.3 s (~40 s longer); lower perceived pain, higher heart rate; fight-or-flight hypothesis. Via paper PDF (UConn mirror) + Medical News Today.
